Graduate Admissions
Graduate Admissions
Graduate Admissions
Application Process
Start Your Graduate Journey
Take the next step toward advancing your career in physics or astronomy at Georgia State University. Below you'll find everything you need to complete your application, including admission requirements, required materials, deadlines, funding information, and contacts for additional guidance. We encourage you to review each section carefully and submit a complete application by the January 15 deadline to receive full consideration for admission and available financial support.
Application process
The Department of Physics and Astronomy welcomes applications to its Astronomy and Physics Ph.D. programs for Fall 2027. We will consider all applications, with preference given to candidates whose research interests and experience closely match the Department's current research strengths. A small number of applications to the Astronomy and Physics M.S. programs will also be considered; however, financial support for master's students is generally limited.
Please complete the online application to apply for graduate studies. Additional application instructions, forms, and links to the online application are available at the College of Arts and Sciences Graduate Admissions website. Applications are accepted for the fall semester only. The deadline is on or BEFORE January 15 each year. Financial aid will be limited and extremely difficult to obtain for spring and summer semester, and granting decision will be made to the most qualified students who apply before the deadline.
If you have questions, please email the relevant Director of Graduate Studies:
For Astronomy, Dr. Misty Bentz, bentz [at] gsu.edu
For Physics, Dr. Xiaochun He, xhe [at] gsu.edu
Admission Requirements
In addition to the general requirements of the College of Arts and Sciences, the Physics & Astronomy has the following additional requirements:
A strong record of coursework and/or experience in a related discipline,
Students with prior relevant laboratory experience will be viewed favorably.
Required Materials
College of Arts and Sciences Application for Graduate Studies
$50 processing fee
Official transcripts (one from each institution attended).
Three letters of recommendation.
International applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English. This may be done by taking the TOEFL or IELTS tests.
Statement of Purpose: See the following tab for advice on how to write an optimal Statement of Purpose.
(Optional) Writing Sample: such as a science-related paper or abstract you’ve written for a college-level course.
Subject GRE scores and General GRE scores are neither required nor used in the applicant evaluation process.
Statement of Purpose
Your personal statement provides you an opportunity to speak directly to the admissions committee; it allows the committee to get to know you through your own words. Strive to write a clear, informative statement that tells the committee about your motivation for and experience with scientific research, how you have collaborated with professors, students or other professionals, and what research tools and methods you have used. Your statement is also the place to explain any weaknesses or inconsistencies in your academic record, if relevant. The committee would like to understand why you want to go to graduate school, and if our program is a good fit for you. Preference is given to applicants with research interests that align well with those of the research faculty, so please indicate research areas in which you are interested and a few research faculty with whom you would potentially like to work. If you are open to alternative research projects, let the committee know that too. Your statement can be up to 2 pages.
Incomplete Applications
If any piece of required information does not reach us by the appropriate deadline, your application may not be considered. Incomplete applications are not returned to the applicant. It is your responsibility to ensure that all material is received by the Office of Graduate Studies, College of Arts and Sciences, by the deadline. You may not be able to control directly when requested transcripts and GRE scores are mailed, thus it is especially important to request such material well in advance of the deadline.
Georgia State University is an equal educational opportunity institution and, as such, students are admitted and treated without regard to race, sex, age, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or disability. The University is in compliance with the regulations for Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.
Financial Policy
The institute expects that graduate students will devote themselves to their studies full time. Accepted Ph.D. students typically receive a stipend and tuition waiver throughout their studies, at a competitive level consistent with their skills and accomplishments. Typically, support involves both research and instructional responsibilities. Students may be eligible to receive funding from other Programs.
Additional information for international applicants
It is recommended that international applicants provide an objective evaluation of their credentials obtained from a credential evaluation service. You can find a list of all of the approved credential evaluation services by going to www.naces.org and clicking on current members. The College of Arts and Sciences accepts evaluations from any of these services.
How to get additional information
Material on our websites should answer most questions. If you have questions for the Office of Graduate Studies, call 404-413-5041, 8:00-5:00 p.m., Eastern Time. If you have questions, you may email the Director of Graduate Studies, Dr. Xiaochun He, xhe [at] gsu.edu (Physics) or Dr. Misty Bentz [at] gsu.edu (Astronomy).
